title: SMP Dallara wins at Le Castellet as United loses its podium
dek: Matevos Isaakyan and Egor Orudzhev won the 4 Hours of Le Castellet for SMP Racing from fourth on the grid, giving the Dallara P217 its first win, as United lost its podium to a post-race penalty.

chapters.title: A title duel on a changed circuit
text: Round four of the 2017 European Le Mans Series, the 4 Hours of Le Castellet on 27 August, came with the LMP2 title fight finely balanced. G-Drive Racing by DragonSpeed's Memo Rojas and Léo Roussel led on 62 points, four ahead of the United Autosports trio of Filipe Albuquerque, Hugo de Sadeleer and Will Owen on 58, with the Oreca and the Ligier JS P217 trading blows all season. High Class Racing's Anders Fjordbach and Dennis Andersen sat third, 28 points off the lead. Behind that sat a field of 12 LMP2 cars split evenly between Oreca 07, Ligier JS P217 and Dallara P217 chassis, four of each.

Several things had changed since the Red Bull Ring. The entry fell to 35 cars after Tockwith Motorsport withdrew from the championship. Paul Ricard also had a new chicane on the Mistral Straight, introduced to slow the faster 2017-spec LMP2 cars, which cost the top class roughly five seconds a lap compared with the old layout. Nicolas Minassian again replaced Ryo Hirakawa, who was on Super GT duty in Japan, in the G-Drive car, while DragonSpeed's second Oreca, the #21 of Ben Hanley, Henrik Hedman and Nicolas Lapierre, arrived looking for redemption after its Red Bull Ring race had ended early. With temperatures soaring, the stewards also prepared a rule allowing a 90-minute stint limit for LMP2 drivers if the official forecast exceeded 32 degrees.

chapters.title: DragonSpeed locks out the front row
text: DragonSpeed had topped every one of its eight practice sessions of the season between its two cars, and Lapierre carried that form into qualifying. His 1:52.761 in the #21 Oreca took pole, with Roussel moving the #22 G-Drive Oreca up to second on 1:52.906, 0.145 seconds slower, after first looking set for third. It was the team's second consecutive front-row lockout.

Enzo Guibbert put the #39 Graff Oreca third on 1:53.051, completing an Oreca sweep of the top three. SMP Racing's Matevos Isaakyan was fourth on 1:53.194 in the #27 Dallara P217, the quickest of the four Dallaras and within half a second of pole. United's Albuquerque was fifth on 1:53.530, the best of the Ligier JS P217 runners, ahead of Giorgio Sernagiotto in the Cetilar Villorba Corse Dallara #47 on 1:53.874 and Nathanaël Berthon in the Panis Barthez Ligier #23 on 1:54.033. Olivier Pla in the IDEC Sport Ligier #28 and Gustavo Yacaman in the second Graff Oreca #40 started ninth and tenth, with the Racing Team Nederland Dallara #29 last on the LMP2 grid.

chapters.title: United spun to the back
text: The race started at noon local time. Hanley in the pole-sitting #21 Oreca and the G-Drive Oreca fought an early battle at the front, but the lap that shaped the title fight happened behind them. United's #32 Ligier was spun on the opening lap in contact with the Cetilar Villorba Corse Dallara, with de Sadeleer saying he had been hit and had no idea what had happened until he saw the replay. The spin cost the car over 30 seconds and left it last in LMP2, a deficit Albuquerque said had destroyed the team's race.

chapters.title: SMP takes control, DragonSpeed fades
text: The first round of pit stops reshuffled the order, and the SMP Racing Dallara moved into the lead, with Isaakyan and Orudzhev leading almost all of the rest of the race. The #21 DragonSpeed Oreca, which had run with the leaders early, faded once Hedman took over the driving. The G-Drive Oreca remained the closest pursuer but could not match the Dallara in the second half, with Roussel fighting poor tyre degradation and ending up in the car for over half of the race.

Behind them United was climbing back from last in class, while Graff's #39 Oreca ran in the podium places and the Panis Barthez Ligier looked strong in the opening hours before a couple of spins slowed it later.

chapters.title: Full Course Yellows decide the strategy
text: The closing stages were shaped by several Full Course Yellow periods. Roussel, who had been within 30 seconds of the SMP Dallara in the final hour, pitted under the second-to-last Full Course Yellow with 22 minutes left for fresh rear tyres, dropped more than a minute behind and held second. SMP, by contrast, used the neutralisations to make only four stops and avoid a final splash. Albuquerque, meanwhile, was catching Graff's Paul Petit for third, and moved ahead in the last hour, and Guibbert's late charge for Graff came up short, leaving the #39 Oreca fourth on the road.

chapters.title: A first Dallara win
text: Isaakyan took the chequered flag after 115 laps, about a minute and a half clear of Roussel's G-Drive Oreca. It was the first win for the Dallara P217 and SMP Racing's first in LMP2, in only the team's second race with the car and the third different LMP2 constructor and team to win in four races this season. Isaakyan said the team had made no mistakes and called the strategy a gamble that worked.

On the road the order behind was G-Drive, United's Albuquerque in third and Graff's #39 Oreca fourth, with the Panis Barthez Ligier fifth. Roussel set the fastest lap of the race, a 1:55.252, and had driven for two hours and ten minutes, longer than planned.

chapters.title: Penalties reshape the podium
text: Post-race, the stewards handed United's #32 Ligier a 30-second penalty for speeds under Full Course Yellow, which dropped Albuquerque, Owen and de Sadeleer from third to fifth. The revised classification promoted the #39 Graff Oreca of Eric Trouillet, Paul Petit and Guibbert to third, the team's second podium of the season, and moved the Panis Barthez Ligier up to fourth. Up to 13 other cars were investigated, and penalties were also given in other classes, but none of them changed the overall order.

The sanction had a direct impact on the championship. G-Drive's lead had stood at seven points on the road result and grew to 12 points over United heading to Spa, once United's result was demoted. Owen later recapped a weekend in which United had first secured the podium and then lost it. DragonSpeed's #21 crew, who had started from pole, finished seventh, one lap down.

For SMP it was a milestone, with a team of open-wheel converts taking its first LMP2 win and the Dallara P217 its first victory, all within two races of the car's debut for the squad. For G-Drive the second place was the key result, as the close Oreca-versus-Ligier title battle turned into a clear 12-point advantage for Rojas and Roussel with two rounds left.
The ELMS now headed to Spa-Francorchamps for the 4 Hours on 24 September, then to Portimão on 22 October for the finale.

facts.v: Nicolas Lapierre took pole with 1:52.761 in the #21 Oreca, 0.145 s ahead of Léo Roussel in the #22 G-Drive Oreca.
